entries.43:13: God says he has been God from ancient times and always will be, and no one can snatch anyone from his hand or reverse what he does. You are safe in God's hands, and his plans cannot be undone.
entries.43:14: God, who defends his people, says that for their sake he will act against Babylon and bring down the Chaldeans. God opposes the powers that hold his people captive.
entries.43:15: God identifies himself as the Lord, the Holy One, the Maker of Israel, and their King. The one who made you also rules over you and is set apart as holy.
entries.43:16: God is described as the one who made a path through the sea and a road through deep waters. The God who rescued his people before is able to make a way for you too.
entries.43:17: God brought out chariots and armies, and they fell and will not rise again, snuffed out like a weak flame. God's power defeats even the strongest forces against his people.
entries.43:18: God tells them not to dwell on the past or keep old times in mind. You don't have to be stuck in past failures or past glories; God is moving forward.
entries.43:19: God says he is doing something new that is already beginning, and he will make a way in the wilderness and rivers in the desert. Watch for God's new work, even in barren places.
entries.43:20: Wild animals will honor God because he provides water in the desert for his chosen people to drink. God provides for his people even in the most unlikely places.
entries.43:21: God says these are the people he made for himself so they would declare his praise. You were made to know God and to speak well of him.
entries.43:22: God says his people have not really prayed to him or thought about him. It is easy to drift into ignoring God even while going through religious motions.
entries.43:23: God says they did not bring him the offerings he asked for, though he never burdened them with excessive demands. God is not asking for exhausting rituals; he wants genuine hearts.
entries.43:24: God says they did not honor him with costly gifts, but instead burdened him with their sins and wrongdoing. Sin weighs on God's relationship with his people, and he calls it out.
entries.43:25: God says he himself wipes away their sins and will not remember their wrongs anymore. God offers real forgiveness that removes your guilt instead of holding it against you.
entries.43:26: God invites them to remind him of their case and argue it, so they can be shown right. God is willing to reason with his people, but honesty is required.
entries.43:27: God says their earliest ancestor sinned and their leaders rebelled against him. Sin runs deep in human history, which is why God's forgiveness matters.
entries.43:28: God says their leaders defiled his holy place, so he brought shame and curse on Jacob and Israel. Leaders' failures affect the whole community, and God takes holiness seriously.
entries.44:1: God is speaking to his people, calling them to listen because they belong to him. It means you should pay attention to God's words since he has claimed you as his own.
entries.44:2: God, who formed each person in the womb, tells his people not to be afraid because he helps them. It means your maker is also your helper, so you don't need to live in fear.
entries.44:3: God promises to pour out water on dry ground and his Spirit on the next generation. It means God brings life and blessing where things feel empty and dry.
entries.44:4: The people will grow and flourish like grass in a watered field. It means God's blessing makes his people thrive and grow strong.
entries.44:5: People will openly identify themselves as belonging to the Lord, using different names for God's people. It means belonging to God will be something people gladly and publicly claim.
entries.44:6: God calls himself the first and the last and says there is no other God. It means God is over all history from beginning to end, and nothing compares to him.
entries.44:7: God challenges any rival to predict the future and explain the past as he does. It means no one else can match God's knowledge and control of history.
entries.44:8: God tells his people not to fear and reminds them they have seen his predictions come true. It means you can trust God because he has proven himself reliable, and he alone is a solid rock.
entries.44:9: Those who make idols gain nothing, and the idols themselves can't see or know anything. It means trusting in things you've made yourself leads to shame and emptiness.
entries.44:10: Anyone who makes a god is really just making a metal image that helps no one. It means handmade gods are worthless and can't do anything for you.
entries.44:11: Everyone involved with idols and secret arts will be ashamed and afraid when they face the truth. It means these practices will ultimately fail and leave people exposed.
entries.44:12: A blacksmith works hard with fire and hammers until he's exhausted and thirsty. It means even the craftsman making a god is weak and human, showing how foolish idol-making is.
entries.44:13: A woodworker carefully shapes a piece of wood into a human figure to put in a house. It means people put great effort into making something to worship that is really just shaped wood.
entries.44:14: The craftsman plants and cuts trees that grow because of rain. It means the material for idols comes from trees God himself makes grow.
entries.44:15: The same wood is used to cook food and keep warm, and then part of it is made into a god to bow down to. It means it's absurd to worship something you'd otherwise burn for heat.
entries.44:16: A person uses part of the wood for a fire, cooks a meal, and feels warm and satisfied. It means the same material used for everyday needs is being treated as a god, which makes no sense.
entries.44:17: The leftover wood becomes a god the person bows to and prays to for rescue. It means people ask a piece of wood to save them, which shows how blind idolatry is.
entries.44:18: Such people lack understanding because their eyes and hearts are closed to the truth. It means idolatry blinds people so they can't see or grasp what's really going on.
entries.44:19: No one stops to think that they used part of the same wood for cooking and now worship the rest. It means people fail to use plain common sense about the things they worship.
entries.44:20: A person deceived like this is chasing dust and can't admit that what they hold is a lie. It means self-deception keeps people from seeing the truth and being saved from it.
entries.44:21: God tells his people to remember these things because they are his servants and he won't forget them. It means you can be confident God remembers you and holds on to you.
entries.44:22: God says he has wiped away his people's sins like a cloud and urges them to return to him. It means God freely forgives and welcomes you back, so you can come to him.
entries.44:23: The heavens, earth, mountains, and trees are called to sing because God has rescued his people. It means God's rescue is such good news that all creation should celebrate it.
entries.44:24: God, who formed you before birth and made everything alone, reminds you he is your redeemer. It means the God who made the universe is personally committed to you.
entries.44:25: God frustrates the predictions of false prophets and exposes the foolishness of those who claim secret knowledge. It means God is greater than any human wisdom or fortune-telling.
entries.44:26: God confirms what his servants say and promises Jerusalem and Judah will be rebuilt and restored. It means God keeps his word and can bring ruined places back to life.
entries.44:27: God commands deep waters to dry up and rivers to stop flowing. It means God has power over even the most impossible obstacles in your way.
entries.44:28: God names Cyrus as the one who will carry out his plan and says Jerusalem and the temple will be rebuilt. It means God can use even a foreign ruler to accomplish his purposes and restore his people.
entries.45:1: God chose Cyrus, a foreign king, and personally strengthened him to defeat nations and open closed doors. This shows God can use anyone, even someone who doesn't know him, to carry out his plans.
entries.45:2: God promises to go ahead of Cyrus and clear every obstacle, smashing through gates and bars that block the way. Whatever seems impossible in your path, God can go before you and make it passable.
entries.45:3: God will give Cyrus hidden treasures stored in darkness, so Cyrus will know it was the Lord who called him by name. God can reveal unexpected provision so that people recognize his hand at work.
entries.45:4: God acts for the sake of his servant Israel, calling Cyrus by name and honoring him even though Cyrus didn't know God. God's plans include people who don't yet know him, and he works for the sake of those he loves.
entries.45:5: God alone is God, and he says he will strengthen Cyrus for battle even though Cyrus doesn't know him. God can equip and use people who have no knowledge of him yet.
entries.45:6: God's purpose is that people everywhere, from east to west, will see that there is no God but him. God's actions are meant to be seen by all, so everyone can know who he is.
entries.45:7: God creates light and darkness, brings blessing and sends trouble; he is behind all of it. Nothing that happens is outside God's control, whether good times or hard times.
entries.45:8: God calls the skies to pour down righteousness and the earth to bring forth salvation like a crop. God himself makes justice and rescue happen, so we can expect him to act.
entries.45:9: It is foolish to argue with your Maker, like a clay pot quarreling with the potter who shaped it. We are the work of God's hands, so we should not challenge what he makes or does.
entries.45:10: It is wrong to question a father about the child he is bringing into life, or a mother about the child she is bearing. Questioning God about what he creates shows a lack of trust in his wisdom.
entries.45:11: The Holy One of Israel, who made all things, asks whether people will question him about the future or give him orders about his children and his work. God is the Maker, not the one who takes orders from us.
entries.45:12: God made the earth, formed people on it, stretched out the heavens by his own hands, and set the stars in their places. The one who made everything has the right to direct it.
entries.45:13: God raised up Cyrus to straighten the way, rebuild his city, and free his captives without payment. God can use a ruler to accomplish his purposes and set people free.
entries.45:14: Egypt, Ethiopia, and distant Sabea will come over to Israel, bow down, and confess that God is with them and there is no other. People from far nations will one day recognize the true God among his people.
entries.45:15: God is described as a God who hides himself, yet he is the Savior of Israel. God doesn't always make himself obvious, but he is still the one who saves.
entries.45:16: Everyone who opposes God will be ashamed and humbled, and those who make idols will be disgraced. Trusting in anything other than God ends in shame.
entries.45:17: God will save Israel with an everlasting salvation, and his people will never be put to shame. God's rescue of his people is permanent, not temporary.
entries.45:18: The Lord made the heavens and designed the earth, not to be empty but as a place for people to live. God made the world with purpose, and he alone is God.
entries.45:19: God did not speak in secret or tell Israel to seek him in a barren wasteland; he speaks truth and what is right. God is open and honest with his people, not hiding his will from them.
entries.45:20: God calls the surviving nations to gather and come near, pointing out that those who pray to wooden idols know nothing and gain no salvation. Idols cannot save, so people should turn to the living God.
entries.45:21: God invites the nations to present their case and debate, asking who foretold these things long ago; he alone did, and there is no God but him. God alone knows and declares the future, and he alone is a true Savior.
entries.45:22: God calls people from every corner of the earth to turn to him and be saved, because he alone is God. Salvation is offered to everyone, everywhere, and it comes by turning to God.
entries.45:23: God swears by himself that his word will not change: every knee will bow and every tongue will honor him. One day everyone will acknowledge God, whether they want to or not.
entries.45:24: Only in the Lord will Israel find victory and strength, while all who were angry with him will be shamed and destroyed. Real strength and vindication come from God alone.
entries.45:25: All of Israel's descendants will be declared right with God and will give him glory. God's people will ultimately be vindicated and will praise him for it.
entries.46:1: The Babylonian gods Bel and Nebo are shown as helpless idols being loaded onto animals and carted away. The things people trusted to carry them have become a burden the tired animals must drag.
entries.46:2: These gods cannot even save themselves, let alone their worshippers, and they all go into captivity together. Trusting in anything other than the real God leaves you with nothing to hold onto.
entries.46:3: God calls his people to listen and reminds them he has carried them since the day they were born. You are not a burden he resents; he has been holding you up from the very start.
entries.46:4: God promises that even in old age he will stay the same and keep caring for the people he made. You can count on him to carry you to the end of your life, not just the beginning.
entries.46:5: God asks who anyone could possibly compare to him. No idol, person, or power comes close to being his equal.
entries.46:6: People weigh out gold and silver and pay a craftsman to make it into a god, then bow down to what they paid for. It is foolish to worship something you had to hire someone to make.
entries.46:7: The idol has to be lifted onto shoulders and set in place, and it cannot move or answer when someone cries out to it. A god you have to carry and rescue cannot rescue you.
entries.46:8: God tells his people to remember this and feel ashamed of their foolishness. It is worth stopping to think about what you are actually trusting in.
entries.46:9: God points back to what he has done in history and says plainly that he alone is God and no one is like him. Remembering his past faithfulness gives you reason to trust him now.
entries.46:10: God declares the future before it happens and says his plans will stand and he will accomplish what he intends. History is not out of control; his purposes will be carried out.
entries.46:11: God calls a swift, distant ruler to carry out his plan, and he guarantees it will happen. When God says he will do something, he makes sure it gets done.
entries.46:12: God speaks to those who are stubborn and have given up believing he will do right by them. He invites the discouraged to listen rather than stay stuck in doubt.
entries.46:13: God says his saving help is close and will come soon, and he will rescue his people and give them honor. Help is nearer than it feels, and he will not leave his people disgraced.
entries.47:1: Babylon is told to get down off its throne and sit in the dust like a humbled servant, because its days of luxury and soft living are over. Pride and comfort can be taken away suddenly, so we should not build our identity on them.
entries.47:2: The proud city is pictured doing hard slave work and being publicly stripped of its fine clothes and dignity. Those who exalt themselves will be brought low and shamed.
entries.47:3: God says the shame of Babylon's humiliation will be seen by everyone, and this time he will not hold back punishment. God's justice is real, and no one who refuses to humble themselves escapes it.
entries.47:4: In the middle of this judgment comes a reminder of who God is: the one who defends his people and commands heaven's armies. The God who judges is also the God who rescues those who belong to him.
entries.47:5: Babylon will sit silent in darkness and lose its famous title as queen of the nations. Earthly glory and reputation do not last.
entries.47:6: God used Babylon to punish his own people, but Babylon went far beyond what was right, showing no mercy and crushing even the elderly. God notices cruelty, especially toward the weak, and holds those who inflict it accountable.
entries.47:7: Babylon assumed its power would last forever and never thought about the consequences of its actions. Assuming tomorrow will be like today is dangerous; we should consider where our choices lead.
entries.47:8: Babylon lived only for pleasure and felt completely safe, telling itself it was unmatched and would never lose what it loved. Self-confident security that ignores God is a trap.
entries.47:9: In a single day Babylon will lose both its husband and its children, despite all its magic and spells. Nothing—not wealth, power, or occult arts—can shield us from God's judgment.
entries.47:10: Babylon trusted in its own wrongdoing and thought no one, not even God, saw what it did, letting its own cleverness lead it astray. We deceive ourselves when we believe our wrongs are hidden.
entries.47:11: Disaster will strike Babylon suddenly, and no amount of money or cleverness can buy it off. Some consequences cannot be avoided once we have chosen evil.
entries.47:12: God mockingly invites Babylon to keep using its magic and spells to see if they can save it. The things we trust instead of God will ultimately fail us.
entries.47:13: Babylon's many advisers—astrologers and stargazers—are told to step forward and save it if they can. Human wisdom and fortune-telling cannot rescue anyone from God's judgment.
entries.47:14: The astrologers are like dry straw that burns up in the fire and cannot even save themselves, let alone anyone else. False sources of security collapse completely when trouble comes.
entries.47:15: The merchants and allies who profited from Babylon for years will all run away, leaving it with no one to save it. People who use us for gain will not stay when we fall.
entries.48:1: God speaks to people who carry Israel's name and swear by him, yet their worship is not honest or sincere. It warns the reader that using God's name while living falsely is empty.
entries.48:2: These people claim to belong to God's holy city and trust in him, calling him the Lord of armies. The reader is reminded that claiming God while ignoring him is not real trust.
entries.48:3: God says he announced things long ago and then suddenly made them happen. This shows he is in control of history and keeps his word.
entries.48:4: God describes these people as stubborn, with a hard heart and an unyielding neck and forehead. It means the reader should not be stiff-necked and resistant to God.
entries.48:5: God told them ahead of time so they could not credit their idols for what happened. It warns the reader not to give false gods credit for what God does.
entries.48:6: They heard and saw these things, so they should testify to them, and now God tells of new and hidden things they did not know. The reader is called to pay attention to what God reveals.
entries.48:7: These new things are happening now, not long ago, so no one can say they already knew. It shows God acts freshly and cannot be predicted or claimed as our own knowledge.
entries.48:8: God says they never truly heard or knew, because their hearts were turned against him from the start. It reminds the reader that a stubborn heart keeps us from truly receiving God's word.
entries.48:9: God holds back his anger and does not destroy them, for the sake of his own name and praise. The reader can see that God's mercy flows from who he is, not from our merit.
entries.48:10: God says he has tested them like silver refined in fire and trouble. It means hard times can be God's way of purifying the reader's faith.
entries.48:11: God acts for his own name's sake and will not share his glory with anyone else. The reader is reminded that God's honor, not our comfort, is the deepest reason for what he does.
entries.48:12: God calls Jacob and Israel to listen, saying he alone is the first and the last. The reader is to hear that God is eternal and there is no one like him.
entries.48:13: God's own hand laid the earth's foundation and stretched out the heavens, and at his word they stand. It means the reader can trust the Creator's word to be powerful and reliable.
entries.48:14: God gathers them to listen and asks who foretold these things, then says his loved one will carry out his purpose against Babylon. The reader sees that God directs even the rise and fall of nations.
entries.48:15: God says he himself called and brought this one and made his plans succeed. It shows the reader that God's purposes are not frustrated but accomplished.
entries.48:16: The speaker says he did not speak in secret and was there from the beginning, and now the Lord God has sent him with his Spirit. The reader is pointed to one sent by God to speak his truth.
entries.48:17: The Lord, who defends Israel, says he is their God who teaches them what is best and guides them in the right way. The reader is invited to trust God's teaching as loving guidance.
entries.48:18: God wishes they had listened to his commands, because then their peace would flow like a river and their goodness like sea waves. It shows the reader that obedience brings deep, lasting peace.
entries.48:19: If they had listened, their descendants would have been countless like sand and their name would never be cut off. The reader sees that listening to God blesses not only us but those who come after.
entries.48:20: God tells them to leave Babylon and flee, announcing with singing to the ends of the earth that the Lord has rescued his servant Jacob. The reader is called to leave bondage and openly tell others of God's rescue.
entries.48:21: When God led them through the desert they did not thirst, because he split the rock and water poured out. It reminds the reader that God provides for his people even in the hardest places.
entries.48:22: God says there is no peace for those who do evil. It is a sober warning to the reader that lasting peace is not possible while we cling to wrongdoing.
entries.49:1: God is calling distant nations to listen. The speaker says God chose and named him before he was even born, meaning God's plans for a person start before birth.
entries.49:2: God made the speaker's words powerful like a sharp sword and kept him safe and hidden like a polished arrow. It means God gives people purpose and protects them for his work.
entries.49:3: God tells the servant that he belongs to God and will show God's greatness to others. The reader is reminded that their life can display God's glory.
entries.49:4: The servant feels his hard work has been pointless, but he trusts God to judge fairly and reward him. It's honest about discouragement while leaving the outcome with God.
entries.49:5: God formed this servant from birth to bring his people back to him, and God honored him and gave him strength. It shows God prepares and strengthens people for the task he gives them.
entries.49:6: God says restoring Israel alone is too small a task; he will also make the servant a light so salvation reaches the whole world. It means God's rescue is meant for everyone, not just one group.
entries.49:7: God speaks to someone despised and rejected by rulers, promising that kings will one day rise and bow because God is faithful. It encourages readers that God honors those the world looks down on.
entries.49:8: God promises to answer and help at the right time, to protect his servant, and to restore ruined land and inheritances. It means God's help comes at the proper moment and brings restoration.
entries.49:9: God tells prisoners to come out free and people in darkness to step into light, and promises food and pasture along the way. It means God leads people out of bondage and provides for their journey.
entries.49:10: Those God leads will not go hungry or thirsty or be harmed by heat, because a merciful God guides them to water. It means God personally cares for and guides those he rescues.
entries.49:11: God promises to turn mountains into roads and raise up highways. It means obstacles that seem impossible will be cleared for God's people to travel.
entries.49:12: People will come from far away, from north, west, and distant lands. It shows God's gathering reaches across the whole world.
entries.49:13: Heaven, earth, and mountains are called to sing because God comforts his people and shows mercy to the crushed. It invites the reader to celebrate God's care for the hurting.
entries.49:14: Zion complains that God has abandoned her and forgotten her. It gives voice to the real feeling that God has left us alone.
entries.49:15: God asks whether a mother could forget her nursing baby, then says even if she could, he will not forget his people. It assures the reader that God's memory and love are more reliable than anyone's.
entries.49:16: God says his people's names are carved on his hands and their walls are always before him. It means God constantly remembers and watches over them.
entries.49:17: The people who rebuild will come soon, and those who destroyed the city will leave. It promises that restoration will come and enemies will depart.
entries.49:18: God tells his people to look around at all who are gathering to them and promises to wear them like jewelry, like a bride dressed for her wedding. It means the returning people will be a source of pride and joy.
entries.49:19: The ruined land will become too small for the number of people, and the destroyers will be far away. It pictures overwhelming restoration after devastation.
entries.49:20: Children born during exile will say there isn't enough room and ask for more space. It shows the surprising growth of God's people beyond what seemed possible.
entries.49:21: Zion wonders who gave her all these children when she had lost hers and felt alone. It expresses amazement at God restoring what seemed permanently gone.
entries.49:22: God signals to the nations, and they will carry his people's sons and daughters home on their shoulders and animals. It means God will use even foreign nations to bring his people back.
entries.49:23: Kings and queens will care for God's people and bow before them, proving that God is real and hope in him is never wasted. It promises honor for the humbled and certainty for those who trust God.
entries.49:24: The question asks whether plunder can be taken from a strong warrior or captives freed from a cruel tyrant. It sets up the seeming impossibility of rescue from powerful oppressors.
entries.49:25: God answers that yes, captives will be taken from the strong and plunder from the cruel, because he fights for his people and protects their children. It means no power is too strong for God to overcome.
entries.49:26: God says attackers will turn on each other, and everyone will see that the Lord is the savior and defender of his people. It means God will decisively rescue his people and make his power known.
entries.50:1: God says Israel was not thrown out like a wife discarded without reason or sold off to pay a debt; the people brought trouble on themselves by their own wrongs. The reader should see that separation from God comes from our own sin, not from God being unfair.
entries.50:2: God asks why no one answered when he came to help, and insists his power has not shrunk—he can still dry up seas and rescue his people. The reader should not doubt God's ability to save just because no one seems to respond.
entries.50:3: God controls even the sky, able to darken it and cover it like sackcloth. The reader should remember that all of creation is under God's command.
entries.50:4: The speaker, God's servant, says God taught him what to say so he can encourage tired people, and he listens to God every morning. The reader should value daily listening to God so they can speak helpful words to others.
entries.50:5: The servant did not rebel or turn away from what God told him. The reader should aim for the same willing obedience.
entries.50:6: The servant willingly accepted beatings, hair-pulling, and insults without hiding his face. The reader should see that faithful service to God can mean suffering patiently rather than fighting back.
entries.50:7: Because God helps him, the servant stands firm like rock and trusts he will be proved right in the end. The reader can face hard times with confidence when God is their helper.
entries.50:8: God, who defends him, is close by, so the servant invites any accuser to come forward and settle the matter. The reader should trust that God is near to defend them against false charges.
entries.50:9: Since God is his helper, no one can rightly condemn him, and his opponents will wear out like old clothes. The reader should not fear human judgment when God is on their side.
entries.50:10: Anyone who respects God but is walking through darkness with no light should keep trusting and relying on the Lord. The reader can hold on to faith even when life feels dark and directionless.
entries.50:11: Those who make their own fire and light instead of trusting God will end up lying down in sorrow. The reader should not rely on self-made schemes to get through life, because that path leads to pain.
entries.51:1: God speaks to people who genuinely want to do right and are seeking him. He tells them to remember where they came from—their humble origins—and to trust that God can build something from small beginnings.
entries.51:2: God points them to Abraham and Sarah, reminding them that Abraham was just one person when God called him. God kept his promise and made a great nation from that single man, so the readers can trust God to do the same for them.
entries.51:3: God promises to comfort his ruined city and turn its desolation into something beautiful like a garden. What was destroyed will be filled with joy, praise, and music again.
entries.51:4: God calls his people to listen carefully because his teaching and his truth will go out to all nations as a light. What God teaches is meant to guide the whole world, not just one group.
entries.51:5: God says his rescue is coming soon and will shine out for everyone to see. Even distant lands and peoples will wait for him and put their hope in his power.
entries.51:6: God tells them to look at the sky and the earth, because both will wear out and pass away like old clothes. But his salvation and his right way of doing things will last forever, so that is where their hope should be.
entries.51:7: God speaks to those who know what is right and have his teaching in their hearts. He tells them not to be afraid of people's insults or threats, because those words don't have the final say.
entries.51:8: People who mock will wear out and be destroyed like a coat eaten by moths. But God's righteousness and salvation will last for all generations, so his people can count on him.
entries.51:9: The people cry out to God to wake up and show his strength, as he did long ago. They remember how he defeated the great sea monster and crushed the powers that opposed him.
entries.51:10: They recall how God dried up the sea and made a path through deep waters. He did this so his people could cross over and be free.
entries.51:11: Those God sets free will come back to Zion singing, with lasting joy on their heads. Sorrow and grief will be gone forever, replaced by gladness.
entries.51:12: God himself says he is the one who comforts them. He asks why they are so afraid of mere humans, who are as temporary as grass and will soon fade away.
entries.51:13: They had forgotten the Lord who made the heavens and the earth, and lived in constant fear of an oppressor. God asks where that oppressor's fury has gone now—it has come to nothing.
entries.51:14: The prisoner bent under chains will soon be set free and will not die in the dungeon. He will have enough food and will not run out.
entries.51:15: God reminds them who he is: the Lord their God, who calms the roaring sea. His name is the Lord of hosts, meaning he commands all powers.
entries.51:16: God says he has put his words in his servant's mouth and shelters him under his hand. The same God who stretched out the heavens and founded the earth declares to Zion, 'You are my people.'
entries.51:17: Jerusalem is told to wake up from the stupor of God's anger, which she has drunk like a cup of wine. She has fully experienced his judgment and needs to rouse herself.
entries.51:18: Among all her children, there is no one left to guide her or take her by the hand. She is utterly alone with no one to help her.
entries.51:19: Two disasters have struck her: ruin and destruction, famine and sword. God asks who will mourn for her and who can comfort her in such devastation.
entries.51:20: Her sons have collapsed like an animal caught in a net, overwhelmed by the Lord's anger and punishment. They are helpless under God's judgment.
entries.51:21: God now speaks to those who are stunned and overwhelmed—not from wine, but from suffering. He calls them to listen to what he is about to say.
entries.51:22: The Lord, who defends his people, says he is taking the cup of his wrath out of their hand. They will never have to drink that cup of judgment again.
entries.51:23: God will hand that cup of wrath to their cruel oppressors instead. Those who forced them down and walked over them will now face the judgment themselves.
entries.52:1: God tells Jerusalem to wake up and put on its strength and fine clothes, because nothing unclean will ever enter it again. For the reader, this is a call to shake off defeat and trust that God is restoring what was ruined.
entries.52:2: Jerusalem is told to dust itself off, stand up, and take its rightful place, because the ropes around its neck are already loosened. It means the reader can stop living like a captive, since God has already begun to set them free.
entries.52:3: God says his people were sold for nothing, and they will be freed without anyone paying a price. The reader is reminded that their rescue comes from God's free choice, not from anything they could pay or earn.
entries.52:4: God recalls that his people went to Egypt long ago to find a home, and later Assyria crushed them for no reason. It shows God remembers the unfair suffering of his people and takes their side.
entries.52:5: God asks what he is getting out of this, since his people were carried off for nothing and their captors mock his name all day. The reader can be sure God sees when his name and people are treated with contempt, and he will act.
entries.52:6: God promises that his people will finally know his name and recognize that he is the one speaking to them. For the reader, it means God is not distant; he makes himself known to those who belong to him.
entries.52:7: The person who brings good news of peace and salvation is called beautiful as they come over the mountains. It means the reader should value those who announce that God is in charge, and can be one of them.
entries.52:8: The watchmen of Jerusalem shout and sing together because they will see the Lord returning to Zion with their own eyes. It means God's return brings joy that people share together, not just privately.
entries.52:9: The ruined places of Jerusalem are told to sing, because the Lord has comforted his people and defended their cause. The reader can take heart that God brings comfort and stands up for those who have been brought low.
entries.52:10: The Lord has shown his power to all nations, and the whole earth will see his salvation. It means God's rescue is not a private matter but something the whole world will witness.
entries.52:11: God's people are told to leave their place of captivity and not carry anything unclean with them, especially those who handle the Lord's equipment. The reader is called to walk away from what defiles them and keep their life clean before God.
entries.52:12: They will not leave in a rushed panic, because the Lord goes ahead of them and guards them from behind. It means the reader can move forward calmly, knowing God leads and protects on every side.
entries.52:13: God points to his servant, who will succeed in what he does and be raised to great honor. It means God's servant, ultimately Jesus, wins in the end, so the reader can trust him.
entries.52:14: People were shocked at the servant because his face and body were so disfigured he hardly looked human. It means the servant suffered deeply and was rejected, which shows how far God's servant went for us.
entries.52:15: Nations and kings will be stunned into silence and honor him, because they will see and understand what they had never been told. It means people who never heard of God's servant will still be moved by what he did.
entries.53:1: People heard the message, but few believed it, and God's power was not obvious to them. It reminds the reader that hearing God's word and actually trusting it are two different things.
entries.53:2: The servant grew up unimpressive, like a weak shoot in dry ground, with nothing attractive to draw people to him. It means God's chosen one may not look impressive or important to us.
entries.53:3: He was rejected, mocked, and avoided, and people treated him as worthless. The reader is warned that we can easily dismiss someone God values.
entries.53:4: He carried our suffering and sickness, yet people assumed he was being punished by God. It means the pain he bore was ours, not his own fault.
entries.53:5: The punishment that brought us peace fell on him. Healing comes at his cost, not at ours.
entries.53:6: Everyone has wandered off like stray sheep, each going their own way, and God laid the guilt of us all on him. It means our wrong choices are real, and someone else bore the cost.
entries.53:7: He was treated harshly but stayed quiet and gentle, like a lamb being led to slaughter. It shows patient, silent endurance instead of fighting back.
entries.53:8: He was denied justice and killed, and hardly anyone cared about his fate; he died for the sins of the people. It means his death was unfair yet purposeful.
entries.53:9: He was buried among wicked people even though he had done nothing wrong and never lied. It highlights how unjustly he was treated to the very end.
entries.53:10: God allowed his suffering and death, and out of it came life and many spiritual children. It means God can bring good and lasting fruit out of painful loss.
entries.53:11: He will be satisfied because through his suffering many are made right with God, since he carried their sins. It means his sacrifice truly helps people and was worth it.
entries.53:12: He will be honored greatly because he gave his life, was counted among wrongdoers, bore the sins of many, and prayed for those who wronged him. It means self-giving sacrifice is rewarded by God.
entries.54:1: God tells his people to sing and celebrate even though they feel empty and abandoned, because he is about to give them far more than they ever lost. The reader can trust that God can bring joy and growth out of a barren, hopeless situation.
entries.54:2: God urges his people to get ready for a much bigger life by expanding their tent and strengthening its stakes. It means the reader should prepare in faith for the growth and room God is going to give.
entries.54:3: God promises that his people will spread out in every direction, gain the nations, and fill empty towns with people. The reader can expect God's blessing to reach beyond them and restore what was ruined.
entries.54:4: God says his people don't need to be afraid of shame or disgrace, because the humiliation of their past will be forgotten. The reader can let go of old shame and sorrow, since God promises a future without them.
entries.54:5: God describes himself as the husband and Maker of his people, the one who defends them and rules over all the earth. The reader belongs to a powerful God who personally takes up their cause.
entries.54:6: God says he is calling back his people like a wife who was sent away in grief, because he does not abandon the one he married long ago. The reader can know that God does not give up on those he has committed himself to.
entries.54:7: God admits he let his people go for a short time, but promises to bring them back with great mercy. The reader can trust that hard seasons are brief compared to the mercy God has for them.
entries.54:8: God says his anger lasted only a moment, but his pity and kindness will last forever. The reader can be sure that God's anger does not last, but his love does.
entries.54:9: God compares his promise to the oath he made after Noah's flood, swearing he will never again be angry with his people or speak bitter words to them. The reader can count on God's promise as firmly as the promise that the flood would never return.
entries.54:10: Even if mountains and hills were to move, God says his love will not leave his people and his peace agreement will not break. The reader can rest in a love that is more solid than the most solid things on earth.
entries.54:11: God speaks to people who are troubled, battered by storms, and without comfort, promising to rebuild them with beautiful, costly stones. The reader who feels crushed can expect God to restore them with care and beauty.
entries.54:12: God promises to decorate the rebuilt city with rubies, sparkling stones, and beautiful walls. It means the reader's restoration will be something lovely and valuable, not just a bare repair.
entries.54:13: God says he will teach all his people, and their children will enjoy great peace. The reader can look for God's own teaching and for peace that reaches their family.
entries.54:14: God promises to make his people secure, so they need not fear evil and destruction will stay away. The reader can live without fear because God himself guarantees their safety.
entries.54:15: God says that if attackers gather against his people, it won't be by his command, and they will fall before them. The reader can trust that enemies rise without God's backing and will not succeed.
entries.54:16: God says he made both the blacksmith who forges weapons and the destroyer who ruins, so he is in control of both. The reader can know that even the tools of harm are under God's authority.
entries.54:17: God promises that no weapon made against his people will work and every accusing voice will be proven wrong, because their right standing comes from him. The reader can stand secure, defended by God against attacks and false accusations.
entries.55:1: God invites anyone who is thirsty or broke to come and receive what they need for free. You don't have to earn or pay for God's help; you just come to him.
entries.55:2: It's a waste to spend your effort on things that never really satisfy you. God asks you to listen to him so you can enjoy what is truly good.
entries.55:3: God asks you to pay attention and come to him, and he promises real life and a lasting agreement of faithful love. Listening to God is how your soul comes alive.
entries.55:4: God made David a witness and leader for the peoples. It shows God's plan to guide the nations through the leader he chooses.
entries.55:5: People you never knew will come running to you because of what the Lord your God has done. God's glory draws outsiders in, not just insiders.
entries.55:6: Look for the Lord now, while he can be found, and pray while he is close. Don't put off turning to God, because the moment to seek him is now.
entries.55:7: Wicked people should stop doing wrong and turn back to God, who will freely forgive them. No matter what you've done, God is ready to show mercy.
entries.55:8: God says his thoughts and ways are not like ours. Don't assume God thinks the way you do; expect him to be different and greater.
entries.55:9: Just as the sky is far above the earth, God's ways and thoughts are far above ours. Trust that God sees and understands far more than you can.
entries.55:10: Rain and snow come down and don't return until they've watered the ground and made it grow food. God's word works the same way in the world.
entries.55:11: God's word never comes back empty; it always accomplishes what he sends it to do. You can count on what God says to actually happen.
entries.55:12: You will leave with joy and be led along in peace, and even nature will celebrate. God's rescue brings gladness that spills over into everything around you.
entries.55:13: Where thorns and brambles grew, beautiful trees will take their place as a lasting sign of what God has done. God turns what is painful and useless into something good that lasts.
entries.56:1: God tells his people to live honestly and treat others fairly, because he is about to act and rescue them. Readers should take their daily conduct seriously since God's help and justice are close at hand.
entries.56:2: A person is truly blessed when they live rightly, rest on the Sabbath as God set it apart, and refuse to do wrong. It means real happiness comes from ordering your life around God's ways, not just knowing about them.
entries.56:3: Foreigners who have joined God's people and men unable to have children should not fear being excluded or written off as worthless. God is telling anyone who feels like an outsider that they are not shut out from him.
entries.56:4: God promises to honor those who cannot have children if they keep his Sabbaths, set their hearts on pleasing him, and stay faithful to their covenant with him. Faithfulness, not family status, is what God looks at.
entries.56:5: God will give these faithful people a lasting place and a name in his house that is better than having sons and daughters, a name that will never be erased. It means belonging to God gives a permanent identity that no circumstance can take away.
entries.56:6: Foreigners who commit themselves to the Lord, worship him, serve him, keep the Sabbath, and hold to his covenant are fully welcomed. God accepts anyone who sincerely turns to him, regardless of where they come from.
entries.56:7: God will bring these outsiders to his holy mountain and give them joy in his house of prayer, accepting their offerings because his house is meant to be a place of prayer for all nations. It means God's welcome is wide open to everyone who comes to him.
entries.56:8: The Lord, who gathers the scattered people of Israel, says he will gather still others besides those already brought back. It means God's rescue plan is bigger than one nation and includes people from outside.
entries.56:9: God calls wild animals to come and feast, picturing judgment coming on a people whose leaders have failed. It is a warning that neglect and corruption will not go unpunished.
entries.56:10: Israel's watchmen, the leaders meant to guard the people, are blind and know nothing; they are like silent dogs that cannot bark, lying around dreaming and loving sleep. It means leaders who fail to warn and protect the people are useless to those they should be guarding.
entries.56:11: These leaders are like greedy dogs always hungry for more, and they lack wisdom, each chasing personal pleasure and profit with no difference between them. It warns that self-serving leaders harm the people they are supposed to care for.
entries.56:12: These leaders say, come, let's get wine and drink heavily, and tomorrow will be just as full of pleasure as today. It shows how far they have fallen, living for indulgence and assuming nothing will ever change.
entries.57:1: Good people die and nobody notices or cares, and God-fearing people are taken away before trouble gets worse. It means the reader should not assume God has forgotten the righteous just because the world ignores them.
entries.57:2: Those who die this way find rest and peace, each one lying down in honor. It means death for the faithful is not a loss but a resting place with God.
entries.57:3: God now speaks to people who practice witchcraft and come from a line of adultery and prostitution. It means the reader should see that dabbling in the occult and sexual betrayal is serious before God.
entries.57:4: God asks who they think they are mocking with their open mouths and tongues sticking out. It means the reader should not treat God or his messengers with sneering contempt.
entries.57:5: They burn with lust under trees and kill children in the valleys and under rocks. It means the reader should recognize that idol worship and child sacrifice are evil, not devotion.
entries.57:6: They treat smooth stones as their inheritance and pour out offerings to them. It means the reader should not give to created things the worship that belongs to God alone.
entries.57:7: They set up their bed on a high mountain and go there to offer sacrifices. It means the reader should see that worshiping in the wrong place and way is still unfaithfulness to God.
entries.57:8: They put their symbols on doors and pillars and made a wide bed with others, making a deal with them. It means the reader should not let secret compromises and divided loyalties replace wholehearted commitment to God.
entries.57:9: They went to Molech with oil and perfume and sent messengers far away, going as low as the grave. It means the reader should see how far people will go chasing false gods, and that it leads downward, not up.
entries.57:10: They wore themselves out on long journeys but refused to say there was no hope, finding new strength instead. It means the reader should notice that stubborn persistence in sin is not the same as real hope.
entries.57:11: God asks whom they feared so much that they lied and forgot him, because he had been quiet and they stopped fearing him. It means the reader should not mistake God's patience for his absence.
entries.57:12: God will expose their supposed righteousness and their deeds, and they will gain nothing from them. It means the reader should not trust in self-made goodness, because it will not stand when God examines it.
entries.57:13: Their false gods will not save them when they cry out; they will blow away like wind, but those who hope in God will inherit the land and his holy mountain. It means the reader should put hope in God alone, since only that hope lasts.
entries.57:14: God commands that the way be raised up and cleared of stones for his people. It means the reader can expect God to remove obstacles and make a path for those he is bringing back.
entries.57:15: The high and holy God, whose name is Holy, also lives with the crushed and lowly in spirit to revive them. It means the reader who feels broken can know that God is near and wants to lift them up.
entries.57:16: God will not stay angry forever, because breath and souls come from him. It means the reader can trust that God's correction has a limit and his purpose is to give life.
entries.57:17: God was angry at their evil and punished them, hiding his face, yet they kept turning their hearts away. It means the reader should not keep resisting God when he disciplines, because that only deepens the distance.
entries.57:18: God has seen their ways and will heal them, give them rest, and comfort them and their mourning people. It means the reader can bring their failures to God and find healing rather than only judgment.
entries.57:19: God creates praise on their lips and announces peace to those near and far, and he will heal them. It means the reader can receive God's peace as a gift that produces thankful words.
entries.57:20: The wicked are like a restless sea that keeps churning up mud and muck. It means the reader should see that sin never settles into peace, no matter how much it tosses about.
entries.57:21: God says plainly that there is no peace for those who do evil. It means the reader should not expect calm and wholeness while holding on to wrongdoing.
entries.58:1: God tells the prophet to speak up loudly and not hold back, pointing out plainly the wrongs and sins of his people. It means God wants honesty about wrongdoing, and it reminds the reader that being told the truth about our faults is meant to help us, not harm us.
entries.58:2: The people act eager for God, praying daily and enjoying learning his ways, as if they were a righteous nation that never abandoned his rules. It means it is possible to look devoted to God on the outside while something is still wrong, so the reader should check whether their devotion is genuine.
entries.58:3: The people complain that they fast and humble themselves but God does not notice, while at the same time they treat the fast day as a chance to do business and press their debtors. It means God sees when religious practice is mixed with unfair treatment of others, so the reader should not expect God to be impressed by rituals while they treat people badly.
entries.58:4: Their fasting ends in quarreling and violence, so their religious days do not reach God's ears at all. It means God is not moved by religious activity that goes along with anger and fighting, and the reader should examine whether their worship is matched by how they treat people.
entries.58:5: God asks whether this is really the kind of fast he wanted, just bowing the head and wearing rough cloth and sitting in ashes. It means God is not satisfied with outward shows of sorrow that change nothing, and the reader should not confuse looking humble with actually being right with God.
entries.58:6: God says the fast he wants is to free people who are wrongly imprisoned, untie the ropes of oppression, and let the crushed go free. It means real devotion to God shows up in setting people free from what holds them down, and the reader should ask what unfair burden they could help lift.
entries.58:7: God's kind of fast means sharing your food with the hungry, sheltering the homeless poor, clothing the naked, and not turning away from your own people in need. It means God measures devotion by practical generosity, and the reader should look for real needs nearby they can meet.
entries.58:8: If you do these things, light will break on you like dawn, your healing will come quickly, and God's glory will follow behind you. It means doing right by others brings God's light and restoration, and the reader can expect God to meet them as they act justly.
entries.58:9: Then when you call, God will answer and say he is here, especially if you stop oppressing others, stop pointing the finger in blame, and stop speaking harmful words. It means God is near to those who treat others fairly and speak kindly, and the reader should watch their treatment of people and their words.
entries.58:10: If you give yourself to feeding the hungry and helping the troubled, then your darkness will turn to light and your night will be like noon. It means generosity toward those in need brings light into your own life, and the reader should expect their own struggles to look different when they care for others.
entries.58:11: God will guide you always, give you water in dry places, strengthen your bones, and make you like a well-watered garden and a spring that never runs dry. It means God sustains those who live generously, and the reader can trust God to keep them going even in hard, dry seasons.
entries.58:12: Your people will rebuild the old ruins and restore foundations from long ago, and you will be called the one who repairs broken walls and makes paths usable again. It means faithful, generous living leaves a lasting mark by restoring what was broken, and the reader can be part of rebuilding their community.
entries.58:13: If you treat the Sabbath as a delight and honor it by not doing business or chasing your own pleasure or talking carelessly on that day, you are showing respect to God. It means setting aside a day for God is meant to be a joy, not a burden, and the reader should guard that time from being swallowed by work and self-interest.
entries.58:14: Then you will find your delight in the Lord, and he will lift you to high places and give you the inheritance promised to Jacob. It means putting God first brings deep joy and lasting blessing, and the reader can trust that honoring God is worth more than the pleasures they give up.
entries.59:1: God is fully able to save and fully able to hear; nothing is too hard for him. If you feel he is not answering, the problem is not that he has grown weak.
entries.59:2: The real barrier between people and God is their own sin, which hides his face and cuts off the answer. Your wrongdoings, not God's weakness, are what separate you from him.
entries.59:3: The people's hands, lips, and tongues are stained with violence, lies, and deceit. Their whole way of speaking and acting shows how far they have drifted from what is right.
entries.59:4: Nobody is standing up for what is fair or telling the truth; they rely on lies and empty words. Plans built on deceit only produce more trouble and harm.
entries.59:5: Their schemes are as dangerous as snake eggs and spider webs, producing death and poison instead of anything good. What looks like a plan for life turns out to hurt those who take it in.
entries.59:6: All their effort produces nothing that protects or covers them; it is just sin and violence. Busy activity without honesty leaves you exposed and empty.
entries.59:7: They rush toward evil and even enjoy harming innocent people; their thoughts and paths are full of ruin. Their lives show a settled habit of hurting others rather than helping them.
entries.59:8: They do not know the way of peace, and their crooked paths leave everyone who walks them without peace. Wrong ways promise progress but never deliver calm or safety.
entries.59:9: Because of this, justice and right living stay out of reach, and people looking for light find only darkness. When sin rules, hope for better days keeps slipping away.
entries.59:10: They stumble along like blind people groping at a wall, even in broad daylight, and feel as good as dead. Sin leaves people confused and unable to find their way.
entries.59:11: They groan like bears and moan like doves, longing for justice and rescue that never seem to come. Honest grief over what is wrong is real, but it does not fix things by itself.
entries.59:12: Their sins pile up and testify against them, and they know it. Admitting the wrong is the first honest step, even when it is painful.
entries.59:13: They have turned against God, lied to him, and let their words and hearts run wild with deceit. Rebelling against God shows up in both what people say and what they secretly plan.
entries.59:14: Justice is pushed back and honesty disappears from public life; uprightness cannot even get into the town. When truth is missing from society, fairness has nowhere to stand.
entries.59:15: Faithfulness has vanished, and anyone who turns from evil becomes a target for the cruel; God saw this and was displeased that no one stood up for justice. Doing right can make you vulnerable, but God notices and cares.
entries.59:16: God saw that no human was stepping forward, so he acted himself to bring salvation and to uphold what is right. When people fail to help, God does not abandon the cause.
entries.59:17: God arms himself with righteousness, salvation, and just anger, like a warrior putting on armor. He takes the fight for justice personally and steps in to defend what is right.
entries.59:18: God will repay people according to what they have done, showing anger to those who attack him and punishment even to distant lands. No one who does evil escapes his fair response.
entries.59:19: People from east and west will see the Lord's name and glory, because he comes like a powerful rushing river driven by his own wind. God's rescue is not hidden; it will be seen far and wide.
entries.59:20: God will come as a Savior to Zion and turn away sin from his people. He does not just punish evil; he personally comes to rescue and cleanse those who belong to him.
entries.59:21: God makes a lasting agreement: his Spirit and his words will stay with his people and their children forever. What God puts in you is not a temporary gift but a promise that carries on to future generations.
entries.60:1: God is telling his people to wake up and shine because his light and glory have come to them. For the reader, it means you can stop living in the dark and let God's presence brighten your life.
entries.60:2: The world around will be dark and confused, but God's light will shine on his people and be seen through them. For the reader, it means that even when things look bleak, God's glory can be visible in your life.
entries.60:3: People from many nations, even rulers, will be drawn to the light God gives his people. For the reader, it means your life touched by God can attract others to him.
entries.60:4: God tells his people to look around and see their scattered children coming home, brought back with care. For the reader, it means God gathers and restores families and people who feel far away.
entries.60:5: When you see this, you'll be overwhelmed with joy because the riches of the sea and nations will come to you. For the reader, it means God's blessing will bring deep gladness, not fear.
entries.60:6: Caravans from distant lands will arrive with gold and spices, telling of God's great deeds. For the reader, it means people from everywhere will recognize and speak about what God has done.
entries.60:7: Flocks from nearby tribes will be brought and used as pleasing offerings, making God's house beautiful. For the reader, it means your gifts and work can honor God and make his house lovely.
entries.60:8: The prophet asks who these people are, coming like clouds and doves flying home. For the reader, it means God's people return swiftly and naturally to where they belong.
entries.60:9: Ships from far-off coasts bring God's people home with silver and gold, because God has made them beautiful. For the reader, it means God values you and brings you back with honor.
entries.60:10: Foreigners and kings will help rebuild your walls, because God's anger has turned to mercy. For the reader, it means God's discipline doesn't last forever; his mercy brings help and restoration.
entries.60:11: Your gates will stay open day and night so the wealth of nations and their kings can come in. For the reader, it means God's welcome is always open and his blessings keep coming.
entries.60:12: Any nation or kingdom that refuses to serve you will be destroyed and left empty. For the reader, it means resisting God's purposes ultimately leads to ruin.
entries.60:13: The finest trees of Lebanon will be brought to make God's holy place beautiful and glorious. For the reader, it means the best you have can be used to honor God and make his presence beautiful.
entries.60:14: Those who were cruel and mocked you will bow before you, and you'll be called the City of the Lord. For the reader, it means God will vindicate you and give you a new, honorable name.
entries.60:15: Though you were hated and abandoned, God will make you a lasting pride and joy for every generation. For the reader, it means God can turn your rejection into something people celebrate for years.
entries.60:16: You'll be nourished by the wealth of nations and know that the Lord is your Savior and defender. For the reader, it means God himself takes up your cause and provides for you.
entries.60:17: God will replace cheap materials with precious ones and make peace and righteousness your leaders. For the reader, it means God upgrades your life and puts fairness and peace in charge.
entries.60:18: Violence and destruction will be gone from your land, and your walls will be called Salvation and your gates Praise. For the reader, it means God brings safety and turns your life into a place of praise.
entries.60:19: You won't need the sun or moon for light, because the Lord himself will be your eternal light and glory. For the reader, it means God is a constant source of light that never fades.
entries.60:20: Your sun will never set and your moon won't dim, because the Lord is your everlasting light and your sorrow will end. For the reader, it means God's light outlasts every dark season and your grief will finally stop.
entries.60:21: All your people will be righteous and will possess the land forever, as a planting of the Lord for his glory. For the reader, it means God makes you good and gives you a lasting place that reflects his glory.
entries.60:22: The smallest family will grow into a thousand, and a tiny one into a strong nation, and God will do it quickly when the time is right. For the reader, it means God can grow small beginnings into something great, and he keeps his timing.
entries.61:1: The speaker says God's Spirit has chosen and sent him to bring good news to poor people, heal the brokenhearted, and free those held captive. This means God cares about people who are hurting or trapped, and the reader can trust that God's help reaches them too.
entries.61:2: He is sent to announce that God's favor has arrived, along with a day when God will judge wrong, and to comfort everyone who is grieving. The reader can take heart that God notices sorrow and acts on behalf of those who mourn.
entries.61:3: God replaces ashes and grief with joy and praise, so that hurting people become like strong, well-planted trees that honor him. The reader can expect God to turn their sadness into something beautiful that brings him glory.
entries.61:4: Those who were ruined will rebuild the old broken-down places and restore towns that had lain waste for generations. The reader sees that God's restoration is real and lasting, not just a feeling but renewed life and community.
entries.61:5: Foreigners will serve as herders, plowmen, and vine-keepers for God's people. The reader learns that God's blessing will be so complete that even outsiders will help care for his people's needs.
entries.61:6: God's people will be called his priests and servants, fed by the wealth of nations and honored with their splendor. The reader is reminded that God's people are set apart to represent him and will share in his abundance.
entries.61:7: Because they suffered double grief and shame, they will receive double reward in their own land and enjoy lasting joy. The reader can trust that God repays past suffering with more than enough blessing.
entries.61:8: God says he loves fair judgment, hates robbery and wrongdoing, and will faithfully reward his people with an everlasting covenant. The reader can count on God being just and keeping his promises to them.
entries.61:9: Their children will be recognized among the nations as people the Lord has blessed. The reader sees that God's blessing is visible to others and carries on through future generations.
entries.61:10: The speaker rejoices because God has clothed him with salvation and righteousness, like a bride dressed for her wedding. The reader can share in that joy, knowing God himself dresses his people in rescue and right standing.
entries.61:11: Just as a garden makes seeds sprout and grow, God will make righteousness and praise spring up in front of all nations. The reader can expect God to bring about visible good fruit in his people for the world to see.
entries.62:1: God says he will not stay silent or rest until Jerusalem's right standing and rescue shine out clearly for all to see. It means God is committed to making things right for his people, and you can trust that he keeps working on their behalf.
entries.62:2: Other nations and their kings will see how God has set his people right and given them honor, and God himself will give them a new name. It means God's work in your life will be visible to others, and your identity comes from him, not from your past.
entries.62:3: God's people will be like a beautiful crown or royal headpiece held in God's own hand. It means you are precious to God and he displays you with pride, not shame.
entries.62:4: God's people will no longer be called abandoned or their land called a wasteland; instead they will be called God's delight and the land will be called married. It means God takes pleasure in you and claims you as his own, so your old labels of rejection no longer apply.
entries.62:5: Just as a groom rejoices over his bride, God will rejoice over his people like a husband delighting in his wife. It means God is glad about you personally and is deeply committed to you.
entries.62:6: God has stationed watchmen on Jerusalem's walls who never stop calling out, and he tells those who remind him of his promises to keep at it. It means persistent prayer matters, and God wants people who keep praying for his purposes.
entries.62:7: These watchmen should keep pressing God and not let him rest until he makes Jerusalem a place of praise across the earth. It means you can boldly keep asking God to fulfill his promises, knowing he welcomes that persistence.
entries.62:8: God swears by his own power that enemies will no longer take the food and wine his people worked hard to produce. It means God guarantees that what you labor for will not be stolen away by those who oppose you.
entries.62:9: Instead, those who harvest the grain and grapes will eat and drink them and praise God in his holy courts. It means you will enjoy the fruit of your work with gratitude to God, not lose it to others.
entries.62:10: The people are told to go through the gates, clear the road, remove obstacles, and raise a banner for the nations. It means God is making a way for people to come to him, and you can help clear the path for others.
entries.62:11: God announces to the whole earth that the Savior is coming, bringing his reward and the people he has rescued with him. It means rescue is certain because God himself has promised it, and he brings his people with him.
entries.62:12: God's people will be called the holy people, those the Lord has rescued, and the city will be called Sought After and Not Abandoned. It means God gives you a new identity as his own, and you are no longer forsaken.
entries.63:1: This pictures God coming like a mighty warrior from Edom, his clothes stained red, strong and determined to save his people. It reminds the reader that God is powerful and fights for those he has chosen to rescue.
entries.63:2: The question asks why God's clothes look red, like someone who has been stomping on grapes. It sets up the answer that follows about judgment.
entries.63:3: God says he crushed his enemies alone, with no one helping, and their blood stained his clothes. It shows that God's judgment is his own work and no one can stand against it.
entries.63:4: God had set a time for punishing evil and for rescuing his people. It means God does not forget his promises and acts at the right moment.
entries.63:5: God looked for someone to help but found none, so he saved his people by his own power. It tells the reader that God himself is enough, even when no one else steps in.
entries.63:6: God says he crushed the nations in his anger and brought their power down to the ground. It shows that proud human strength cannot last against God.
entries.63:7: The speaker now turns to praise God for his mercy and for all the good things he has done for his people. It invites the reader to remember and speak of God's kindness.
entries.63:8: God called Israel his own people, children who would be faithful, and so he saved them from trouble. It shows that God's care comes from his commitment to his people.
entries.63:9: God did not send an angel but came himself to save them, out of love and pity, carrying them through the years. It tells the reader that God is personally involved in caring for his people.
entries.63:10: But the people rebelled and grieved God's Holy Spirit, so he turned against them. It warns that rejecting God brings real consequences.
entries.63:11: The people remembered the old days with Moses and asked where God was now, the one who brought them through the sea. It shows how longing for God's past help can lead people to pray.
entries.63:12: God used his mighty power through Moses to part the waters and make a lasting name for himself. It reminds the reader that God's great acts are meant to show who he is.
entries.63:13: God led his people through deep waters safely, like a horse crossing open ground. It pictures God guiding his people through danger without letting them fall.
entries.63:14: Like cattle resting in a valley, the people were guided safely by God's Spirit, and he made a great name for himself. It shows that God's leading is gentle and brings his people to rest.
entries.63:15: The people beg God to look down from heaven and show his compassion and power again. It is a prayer for God to act and not hold back his mercy.
entries.63:16: Even if Abraham and Israel forgot them, God is still their father and has always cared for them. It tells the reader that God's fatherly care is more reliable than any human connection.
entries.63:17: The people ask God why he lets them wander and grow hard-hearted, and they plead with him to return for the sake of his servants. It expresses honest confusion and a deep desire for God to bring them back.
entries.63:18: They ask why enemies have trampled on God's holy place. It voices the pain of seeing what is sacred to God treated with contempt.
entries.63:19: The people feel as though they were never God's own, as if his name had never been called on them. It expresses the feeling of being abandoned and the longing to belong to God again.
entries.64:1: The prophet longs for God to tear open the sky and come down in power, so that even the mountains shake at his presence. It invites the reader to desire God's direct action rather than his silence.
entries.64:2: He compares God's coming to fire igniting dry brush or water boiling over, so that his enemies tremble before him. The point is that God's arrival should be unmistakable and make people take him seriously.
entries.64:3: God has done mighty things his people never expected, things no one had heard of before. It reminds the reader that God can act in ways beyond what we anticipate.
entries.64:4: No eye has seen and no ear has heard of any God besides the Lord who acts on behalf of those who wait for him. It encourages the reader to keep trusting and waiting, because God rewards those who do.
entries.64:5: The people ask whether God will help those who delight in doing right and remember his ways, then admit they kept sinning and deserved his anger. It shows honest confession alongside a plea for mercy.
entries.64:6: Everyone has become ritually unclean, and even our best deeds look like a filthy garment; we wither like a dead leaf and our sins blow us away. It tells the reader that no one can stand before God on their own goodness.
entries.64:7: No one calls on God's name or rouses himself to hold fast to him, because God has hidden his face and handed them over to their sins. It warns the reader about the danger of prayerlessness and drifting from God.
entries.64:8: Yet the people address God as their Father, the potter who made them, and themselves as clay and the work of his hands. It gives the reader hope that the one who made us can also remake us.
entries.64:9: They beg God not to stay angry forever or keep holding their sins against them, and they ask him to listen because they belong to him. It models a humble, persistent plea for forgiveness.
entries.64:10: The holy cities lie in ruins, and Jerusalem is a heap of broken walls. It shows the reader the real devastation that sin and judgment bring.
entries.64:11: The holy and beautiful temple where their ancestors praised God has burned, and everything precious to them is destroyed. It expresses grief over lost worship and asks the reader to feel the cost of that loss.
entries.64:12: The prophet closes by asking whether God will still do nothing, stay silent, and let the suffering go on. It gives the reader permission to bring honest, urgent questions to God rather than pretending everything is fine.
entries.65:1: God says he was ready to respond and show himself to people who weren't even looking for him or praying to him. It means God often reaches out first, even to those who ignore him.
entries.65:2: God kept reaching out all day long to a stubborn people who kept going their own wrong way. It shows how patient God is, even when people keep resisting him.
entries.65:3: These people constantly angered God by worshiping in forbidden ways, like making offerings in gardens and burning incense on bricks. It means religious activity done on our own terms, against God's clear direction, offends him.
entries.65:4: They sat among graves and in secret places, ate pork, and used unclean things in their rituals. It describes people deliberately choosing practices God had forbidden.
entries.65:5: They told others to stay away because they thought they were too holy to be touched. God says this self-made holiness disgusts him like smoke in his face all day.
entries.65:6: God says he has recorded all this and will not hold back forever; he will repay. It means God sees wrongdoing and will eventually act justly.
entries.65:7: God will hold them accountable for their own sins and their ancestors' sins, like burning incense on mountains and insulting him on hills. It means sin has consequences that carry across generations unless people turn back.
entries.65:8: Just as people spare a cluster of grapes because good juice is in it, God will spare some of his people rather than destroy them all. It means God preserves a faithful remnant out of mercy.
entries.65:9: God will bring descendants from Jacob and Judah who will inherit his mountains and live there as his people. It means God keeps his promises to his people's future.
entries.65:10: The plain of Sharon and the valley of Achor will become good pasture for flocks and herds belonging to people who turned back to God. It means God restores and provides for those who return to him.
entries.65:11: But those who abandon the Lord and ignore his holy mountain, setting a table for 'Chance' and mixing wine for 'Fate,' are addressed next. It means trusting luck or fate instead of God is a serious betrayal.
entries.65:12: God says these people will fall by the sword because they ignored his call and chose evil. It means refusing to listen to God has real and deadly consequences.
entries.65:13: God's servants will eat, drink, and rejoice, while those who rejected him will go hungry, thirsty, and be put to shame. It means God will reverse the fortunes of the faithful and the unfaithful.
entries.65:14: God's servants will sing from joyful hearts, but the others will cry out from sorrow and brokenness. It means the outcome of following God versus rejecting him is dramatically different.
entries.65:15: The names of those who rejected God will become a curse word among his people, and God will give his servants a new name. It means God will separate the faithful from the unfaithful and give his people a fresh identity.
entries.65:16: People will bless and swear by the true God because past troubles will be forgotten and wiped away. It means God's future restoration will be so complete that old pain no longer defines his people.
entries.65:17: God promises to create new heavens and a new earth, with the former things completely forgotten. It means God's ultimate plan is full renewal, not just patching up the old.
entries.65:18: People will rejoice forever in what God creates, because he will make Jerusalem a delight and its people a joy. It means God's renewal brings lasting gladness, not temporary relief.
